# Does interval probing pay its own cost?

Run the frozen full-interval probing rule on the 14 even-numbered CSPLib curricula at their archived balanced peaks and 32 saved requests each. Prior work already examined these requests with other algorithms. Development of the probing rule used the 14 odd instances. Compare probe plus exact fallback against the same fallback with original precedence windows, both with and without the existing interval screen. Every solver receives tightened domain bounds available to that policy, the same compiled model template, a single worker and three deterministic time units. Include all screen computation and per-request model setup in service times. Build templates and longest-path closures once per curriculum. Record closure preparation separately. Use three fresh shuffled blocks per request; fix each process to one CPU. Check each witness against original constraints and every definite status against independent archived decisions, retaining timeout cases. Report calls avoided, unknowns, per-curriculum ratio of means of request medians and their geometric mean. Practical speed target remains 10% against every control, at full resolution. Preserve the negative result if probes reduce calls but increase end-to-end time.
